policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 24 Apr close (1x4 3.86, 3x6 4.00, 6x9 4.23, 9x12 4.35 vs WIBOR 3M 3.84) price roughly 50bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 9 Apr; Glapiński sees no near-term change either way - hikes only in a 'black scenario' of renewed war, a question mark over cuts. Zarzecki (23 Apr): unchanged for long, any move likely up; Tyrowicz: wages still an inflation risk. March CPI 3.0% (final, 15 Apr; flash 31 Mar, 3.3% expected); core 2.7% (16 Apr). The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 30 Apr (13 Apr).
policy.risk_text: Upside risk to yields: strong March activity and wage data, hawkish MPC voices and ECB/BoE hikes priced keep NBP-hike pricing alive while oil climbs back above $100; a US-Iran deal is the relief valve. Long end: a 2026 deficit of ~6.8% of GDP and weekly supply.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026 (Inflation Report, 6 Mar); the NBP forecaster survey (1 Apr) has 2026 CPI at 2.9%; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The next projection comes in July.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; S&P (2-6 Apr) sees a 2026 deficit of 7.0% of GDP (8.0% in an oil-shock case); budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); the fiscal notification (22 Apr) has a 2026 deficit of ~6.8% of GDP and debt 65.1%; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) to 30 Apr; the EC sent the SAFE loan agreement (23 Apr).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~48% (after 23 Apr, Erste) financed; USD 6bn of 5Y/10Y/30Y priced on 7 Apr (UST +65/+105/+130bp); budget accounts PLN 169.5bn at end-March. No rating action in April; S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut to 3.75% on 4 Mar and held on 9 Apr; March CPI 3.0% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 revised to 4.1%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 24-26 Apr: DS0436 (25 Apr 2036) listed from 28 Apr; March unemployment 6.1%; Erste: ~48% of 2026 needs covered after 23 Apr, rates flat to year-end; the PM wants the SAFE loan kept out of the deficit; the long end rose ~20bp on the week as oil rose (10Y ~5.6%). Abroad: Ifo 84.4 (lowest since 2020); two ECB and two BoE hikes fully priced plus ~50-55% for a third; UMich sentiment 49.8, 1Y expectations 4.7%; Brent ~$105 after Trump cancelled the envoys' trip; S&P cut Belgium to AA- and Slovakia to A.

calendar.plan_text: MoF April plan (31 Mar): sale auctions on 15 Apr (PLN 4-12bn; OK0128, NZ0331, PS0731, DS1035, NZ0936), 23 Apr (6-14bn) and 28 Apr (5-13bn; new 10Y DS0436 replaces DS1035 from 23 Apr); no switch; a 50-week T-bill on 10 Apr (3-6bn). Q2 plan: 7-8 sales for PLN 50-90bn and 1-2 switches. 2026 needs ~41% financed at end-Q1. 7 Apr: USD 6bn issue (5Y 4.645%, 10Y 5.405%, 30Y 6.233%). 10 Apr T-bill: PLN 3.0bn at 3.95% (demand 3.6bn) plus 0.39bn. 15 Apr sale: PLN 10.71bn vs 12.13bn demand (cover 1.13) plus 0.35bn; PS0731 5.023%, DS1035 5.514%, WS0428 4.271%. 23 Apr sale: PLN 8.98bn vs 11.19bn (cover 1.25) plus 1.19bn; DS0436 debut 5.680%, PS0731 5.147%. BGK FPC (16 Apr): PLN 1.06bn sold on 1.89bn demand plus 0.21bn.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it. April is back to regular supply: remaining sales 28 Apr. Next MPC 5-6 May: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker. Covers so far: 1.13 (15 Apr), 1.25 (23 Apr) vs 1.17 on 25 Mar.

facts.core_text: Regime: the oil shock is back (Brent above $100, Bund near 2011 highs) with hawkish repricing abroad; the NBP held at 3.75% on 9 Apr while FRAs price roughly 50bp of NBP hikes; the ECB and BoE are priced for hikes, the Fed is on hold, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 52bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 261bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 24 Apr close). Ifo 84.4; two-plus ECB hikes priced (24 Apr).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: on 16 Apr BGK sold PLN 1.06bn of FPC bonds on 1.89bn demand plus 0.21bn - a first sign of rebuilding demand (PKO); next tender 29 Apr.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
